key_test: independent-samples Student t-test (var.equal), learning = RB12Mean - FSMean, Achievement prime (1) vs Control (2), rows with Include1 = 'Include for analyses'
exclusions: Include1 == 0 ('Include for analyses'): first 79 usable per condition after awareness, technical and 4-SD exclusions

r_script.es: d = -0.1 (compute.es::des on t/sqrt(N) with n1 = n2 = N)
r_script.how: audit script run unmodified through a shim that maps getOSFfile() to the local downloaded copy and skips library(httr), library(RCurl) and the remote source() of getOSFfile.R (no network beyond osf.io)

agreement: t and p: all three agree (|t| 1.318, p .189; the table stores |t| with Direction 'opposite'). Effect size: table -0.21 and Python -0.2097 agree; the R script prints -0.10, wrong by a factor of two because it feeds t/sqrt(N) as d and sets both group sizes to N = 158.
notes: Anchored on the test statistic and p (script, table and Python agree), and on the pooled d for the effect size (script's ES line is wrong). Mean learning prime 22.27 ms vs control 33.11 ms: opposite to the prediction. RB12Mean verified = (R1Mean+R2Mean)/2 exactly; stored 'Learning' is FS - RB, the negative of the analysed score. Welch gives the same t (equal n, near-equal SD).
